results.evidence: Retry searched further Rake/Southern Picket trip reports. The enchainment account and later reports mention only rappelling from the Rake's summit (and separate raps into the Terror col off Mount Terror), never a number of rappels or stations for the Rake itself. The rappels prose ('number unknown') remains the supportable statement; the three-row table is an estimate with no outside support. Settled only by a party that descended the Rake and recorded its stations.

One topo-derived list gives 7,869 ft; the peak-list/Wikipedia-style listing gives 7,840 ft. A USGS 3DEP point-elevation grid of 49 samples around the summit pin peaks at ~7,825 ft (pin itself 7,822 ft), which is below both and cannot adjudicate a sharp spire where the DEM undershoots. Sources genuinely disagree; settled by a surveyed or LiDAR spot height for the summit.

A new trip report describes continuous class 3 with one short exposed move; a club route page says it should never exceed class 3; a scramble blog says class 3/4; a peak page summary calls the summit block easy low fifth class. Still no two sources give the 5.4 crux, and they split between class 3, 4 and low 5th. Settled by two independent parties rating the easiest summit line.

summitTimeHrs (10) equals the whole day-2 section (climb, return to camp and hike out), while the schedule puts the summit ~3-3.5 h from camp. Further trip reports gave no camp-to-summit time. Belongs to the null-not-compute class repair (set summitTimeHrs to null) rather than a sourced value.

results.fact: Mileage to the Snowy Lakes spur
results.evidence: Outside figures for Rainy Pass to the Snowy Lakes junction still scatter: 9.2 mi (one hike write-up), 9.5 mi (PCT section guide), ~10 mi (a trip report's '7 miles to Granite Pass plus 3 more'), and ~10.5 mi (Granite Pass 6.25 + 4.3). The WTA page gives 23 mi round trip to the lakes but no junction figure. No two independent sources agree closely; settled by a GPS track or official PCT mileage for the junction.

Searches for the Fantasy Falls ice line found no page besides the one route page; none state the car-to-base-of-ice gain. The row's own arithmetic (130 m route topping out at 6,971 ft from a ~4,550 ft trailhead) makes '1,500 ft to the base' too low, but no sourced figure exists to replace it. Settled by a trip report stating the base elevation of the ice.

results.correct_value: about 4.8-5 mi round trip (2.4 mi one-way)
results.evidence: The WTA hike page for Unicorn Peak gives 4.8 miles round trip with 2,397 ft gain to 6,971 ft; an independent personal trip report gives c.5 miles round trip and c.2,400 ft gain from the Snow Lake trailhead. These agree with the row's itinerary (4.8 mi RT), approach and descent (2.4 mi one-way) and dist_km; the '6-mile' figure in partner requirements (repeated by a peak page) is the outlier.

Further searching (trip-report forums and blogs) found no source giving a Roman commitment grade for Ares Tower; sources describe a 4th-class spire with a short 5th-class final step, a short-day objective. Neither II-III nor I-II is stated by any source. Settled by a published grade for the Ares Tower standard route.
